statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains low because current evidence does not establish a persistent no-retracement Nasdaq-100 path.
recommendation: Mapped policy state remains EA_ON; the principal conditional risk checkpoint is the U.S. cash open and flash-PMI/post-release sequence.
headline: Low Tail with extreme rates and event stress; the U.S. open and flash PMI remain the main conditional risk window.
body: Reuters reports Nasdaq futures broadly steady in Asia, technology shares firm, oil lower and short Treasury yields elevated. Delayed public NQ pages are not sufficiently consistent for granular live-path claims, so current evidence does not establish repeated failed retracements or persistent one-way structure.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 clock-hour assessments, Tail was mostly low, briefly rose through WATCH and peaked at 27% around the prior U.S. open, then fell as mixed structure and retracement evidence returned. Stress remained high to extreme.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours remain low-Tail in the base case outside a narrow 13:30-15:30 UTC U.S. open/PMI/Fed/EIA window. Forecast Tail rises only conditionally if opening direction persists through shallow pullbacks, failed retracements or a coherent second leg.

forecast.analysis: Current evidence is mixed rather than one-way: Reuters reports Nasdaq futures steady with Asian technology strength, lower oil and firm short yields. Delayed public NQ pages are not consistent enough to verify a failed-retracement sequence, so Tail remains low.
drivers: Nasdaq futures reported broadly steady in Asia
Oil eased while short Treasury yields stayed elevated
Granular live NQ pullback quality is not consistently verified

news.title: Asia stocks ride tech wave higher, oil stays subdued

forecast.analysis: If early-European liquidity keeps futures inside an overnight range, Tail remains low. A sustained break that repeatedly extends with shallow pullbacks would be the main condition for escalation.
drivers: Repeated extension would be the key Tail checkpoint

forecast.analysis: The European cash-market transition can increase directional participation. Tail stays low unless a fresh extreme is held through weak retracements and cross-asset confirmation strengthens.
Early European trading should clarify whether technology-led risk appetite broadens. Tail remains low if two-way trade persists; sustained directional efficiency with weak pullbacks would raise it.
drivers: Pullback depth is the main path test

forecast.analysis: With Europe established, rates and oil become more informative. Softer oil is a partial offset to rate pressure; Tail would need a sustained NQ extreme plus weak retracements to move above low.
U.S. premarket participation begins to matter more. Stress rises ahead of the cash open and flash PMI, but Tail remains low unless a directional pre-open build develops with poor mean reversion.
drivers: Flash U.S. PMI later at 13:45 UTC

forecast.analysis: Late-European positioning can widen swings before the U.S. event cluster. Tail stays low unless futures build persistently in one direction with shallow or failed retracements.
drivers: Retracement quality remains the Tail test

forecast.analysis: As the U.S. open approaches, event and liquidity risk increase. WATCH-level Tail is conditional on futures already holding an extreme or developing a directional pre-open structure that resists retracement.

This hour contains the 13:30 UTC cash open and 13:45 UTC flash PMI. Elevated Tail is conditional on opening-auction direction persisting through shallow pullbacks, failed retracements or repeated extension; the events alone do not establish that path.
drivers: Conditional shallow pullbacks or failed retracements

forecast.analysis: The first full post-PMI hour also includes Governor Barr at 14:05 UTC and the EIA report at 14:30 UTC. Elevated Tail requires a coherent second leg or continued extreme holding; two-way price discovery would argue for rapid de-escalation.

After the main release cluster, Tail falls toward WATCH if retracements reappear and the opening move stops extending. Continued one-way structure through this hour would keep the conditional risk elevated.
drivers: Persistence versus exhaustion of the opening move

forecast.analysis: By the U.S. late morning, the base case shifts toward lower Tail if price discovery becomes two-sided. A second extension after failed retracements would keep WATCH conditions relevant.

Early U.S. afternoon conditions are lower-Tail if the event-driven move has mean-reverted. Persistent near-extreme holding or renewed cross-asset alignment would be the main reason for renewed concern.
drivers: Conditional mean reversion after the event cluster

forecast.analysis: With the scheduled U.S. catalyst cluster behind the market, Tail is expected to stay low unless a delayed second leg develops with repeated extension and weak pullbacks.
Later U.S. trading should favor lower Tail if range formation develops. A late-session break that holds near an extreme without meaningful retracement would be the primary escalation condition.
If the U.S. afternoon remains two-sided, Tail stays low and Stress can ease from the event peak. Only renewed directional efficiency would justify a higher path-risk estimate.
Into the cash close, the base case is normal rather than trend persistence. A closing drive that repeatedly extends without pullbacks would be the exception that raises Tail.
After the U.S. cash close, reduced scheduled-event density favors low Tail. Thin liquidity can amplify moves, but path risk rises materially only if direction persists through failed retracements.
Early overnight trade may be headline-sensitive around geopolitics and rates. Tail remains low unless a headline shock produces sustained one-way structure rather than a reversible gap.
In the Asian overnight window, low Tail remains the base case if futures rotate rather than extend. Persistent extreme holding would be required to shift the regime materially.
drivers: Extreme holding as the escalation test

forecast.analysis: Absent a fresh catalyst, overnight price discovery should remain lower-Stress than the U.S. event window. Tail stays low unless repeated extension appears without meaningful pullbacks.
As Asia matures, the base case remains low Tail with normal two-way structure. A directional move would need cross-asset confirmation and failed retracements to become a stronger concern.
drivers: Failed retracements as the Tail threshold

forecast.analysis: Approaching the next European pre-open, participation can increase again. Tail remains low unless an overnight move reaches and holds an extreme with shallow pullbacks.

The final forecast hour precedes Thursday's U.S. claims and housing data by several hours. Stress can begin to rebuild modestly, while Tail remains low unless live structure is already persistently directional.
drivers: Thursday U.S. data later in the day

forecastDetail.comment: Current mixed evidence supports low Tail: steady futures reporting and softer oil conflict with firm short yields; granular NQ pullback quality is not consistently verified.
Low Tail persists if early-European liquidity preserves a range; repeated extension with shallow pullbacks would be the escalation checkpoint.
European cash participation can increase directionality, but Tail stays low unless a fresh extreme holds through weak retracements.
Early Europe remains mixed; sustained directional efficiency rather than ordinary two-way trade would be required for higher Tail.
Rates and oil provide cross-asset context, while sustained NQ extreme holding and weak retracements remain the necessary Tail evidence.
U.S. premarket participation lifts Stress ahead of the open and PMI; Tail remains low without a persistent pre-open build.
